arml-local-2010-theme-01.title: Cone minus small cone
arml-local-2010-theme-01.body:
Extend the sides of the frustum to the full cone, and let $x$ be the height of the small cone cut off at the top. Similar triangles: $\frac{x}{x+4}=\frac58$, so $x=\frac{20}3$ and the full cone has height $\frac{32}3$. The slant heights are $\sqrt{8^2+(32/3)^2}=\frac{40}{3}$ (full cone) and $\sqrt{5^2+(20/3)^2}=\frac{25}{3}$ (small cone).

Lateral surface area of the frustum: $\pi\cdot8\cdot\frac{40}3-\pi\cdot5\cdot\frac{25}3=\frac{320\pi-125\pi}{3}=65\pi$. Add the circular top, $\pi\cdot5^2=25\pi$: total $90\pi$.

**Answer: $90\pi$ sq km**

arml-local-2010-theme-02.title: Similar triangles
arml-local-2010-theme-02.body:
Put $D=(0,0)$, $A=(5,0)$, $B=(10,0)$, $C=(0,15)$. The bottom-left corner of $S_1$ is $A$ (on $AC$), and the top-right corner $(5+s,s)$ lies on $BC$: $y=15-\frac32x$. So $s=15-\frac32(5+s)$, giving $\frac52s=\frac{15}2$ and $s=3$. (Equivalently $\triangle P_1Q_1B\sim\triangle CDB$ gives $\frac{s}{5-s}=\frac{15}{10}$.)

**Answer: 3 meters**

arml-local-2010-theme-03.title: Place the second square
arml-local-2010-theme-03.body:
Use the coordinates $D=(0,0)$, $A=(5,0)$, $B=(10,0)$, $C=(0,15)$; line $AC$: $y=15-3x$, line $BC$: $y=15-\frac32x$. $S_2$ sits on $S_1$, whose top is at height $3$. Its bottom-left corner is on $AC$ at height $3$: $x=4$. Its top-right corner $(4+s,3+s)$ is on $BC$: $3+s=15-\frac32(4+s)$, so $\frac52s=6$ and $s=\frac{12}5$.

**Answer: $\dfrac{12}{5}$ meters**

arml-local-2010-theme-04.title: Geometric series
arml-local-2010-theme-04.body:
If a square rests with its bottom edge at height $h$, its bottom-left corner on $AC$ at $\left(\frac{15-h}{3},h\right)$ and top-right corner on $BC$ gives $s=\frac{15-h}{5}$. The next square starts at height $h+s$, so $15-h_{n+1}=\frac45(15-h_n)$ and $s_{n+1}=\frac45s_n$ with $s_1=3$.

Total area of the squares: $\dfrac{3^2}{1-\left(\frac45\right)^2}=\dfrac{9}{9/25}=25$. The triangle has area $\frac12\cdot5\cdot15=\frac{75}2$. The fraction is $\frac{25}{75/2}=\frac23$.

**Answer: $\dfrac23$**

arml-local-2010-theme-05.title: Inradius
arml-local-2010-theme-05.body:
$BC=5$ (3-4-5 triangle). $C_1$ is the incircle, so its radius is $\frac{\text{area}}{\text{semiperimeter}}=\frac{\frac12\cdot3\cdot4}{\frac12(3+4+5)}=1$.

**Answer: 1 meter**

arml-local-2010-theme-06.title: Tangent circles along an angle bisector
arml-local-2010-theme-06.body:
Let $\theta=\frac12\angle ACB$. Both centers lie on the bisector of $\angle ACB$, a ray from $C$ making angle $\theta$ with $CA$, so $CO_i=\frac{r_i}{\sin\theta}$. Hence $O_1O_2=CO_1-CO_2=\frac{r_1-r_2}{\sin\theta}$, and external tangency gives $O_1O_2=r_1+r_2$. So $r_1-r_2=(r_1+r_2)\sin\theta$ and $r_2=r_1\frac{1-\sin\theta}{1+\sin\theta}$ with $r_1=1$.

$\cos\angle ACB=\frac45$, so $\sin\theta=\sqrt{\frac{1-4/5}{2}}=\frac1{\sqrt{10}}$ and $r_2=\frac{\sqrt{10}-1}{\sqrt{10}+1}=\frac{(\sqrt{10}-1)^2}{9}=\frac{11-2\sqrt{10}}{9}$.

**Answer: $\dfrac{11-2\sqrt{10}}{9}$ meters**

arml-local-2010-theme-07.title: Track a full rotation
arml-local-2010-theme-07.body:
A full cycle of substitutions (each player sits out once, 11 changes $=33$ minutes) brings player 1 back to the bench. After the first cycle the two teams are $\{11,2,3,4,5\}$ and $\{6,\dots,10\}$: going around the ten players $2,3,\dots,11$ in order, the two blocks of five consecutive players each move one place. After the next cycles the teams are $5$-$9$ (and the rest), then $4$-$8$, $3$-$7$ and finally $2$-$6$ vs $7$-$11$ again, after 5 cycles. Player 1 is only on the bench at the end of a cycle, so the groups $2$-$6$ and $7$-$11$ cannot recur earlier. (A direct simulation of the substitutions confirms this.)

Total time: $5\cdot11\cdot3=165$ minutes.

**Answer: 165 minutes**

arml-local-2010-theme-08.title: Deduce the results
arml-local-2010-theme-08.body:
Each team has played at most three games. The US has 2 wins and 1 draw and, having conceded no goals, no losses: 3 games and $5$ match points. Finland has played 3 games and has 1 match point: 0 wins, 2 losses, 1 draw. So the US and Finland have each played everybody, and Russia (2 games) played exactly them, which leaves Canada with only 2 games (against the US and Finland).

Finland conceded 11 goals over three games and no team scored five goals in more than one game, so each of Finland's three opponents scored against them (otherwise at most $5+4=9$ goals). Since the US conceded no goals, the US-Finland game was not a draw, so Finland's single draw was against Russia. Russia has 2 points from 2 games, so it also drew with the US, and that was $0$-$0$. Russia scored 2 goals in total, so its draw with Finland was $2$-$2$.

Finland's two losses (to the US and Canada) conceded $11-2=9$ goals. Since only one game reached five goals for a team, these were $5$ and $4$. The US conceded no goals, so it did not win $5$-$1$; hence Canada beat Finland $5$-$1$ and the US beat Finland $4$-$0$. The US's other win is over Canada, and by the clue its two winning margins differ by one: the margin is $3$ (a margin of $5$ would need a second five-goal game), so the US beat Canada $3$-$0$. Now the totals are: US $4+3+0=7$ goals for, $0$ against; Canada $0+5=5$ for, $3+1=4$ against; Finland $0+1+2=3$ for.

The completed chart is shown in the answer.

**Answer:** see the completed table.

arml-local-2010-theme-09.title: Reconstruct the tournament
arml-local-2010-theme-09.body:
There are 10 matches in all, so the number played is $3$, $5$ or $7$ (a prime, with a prime number remaining). Three matches have at most $15$ goals, fewer than the 17 required, so not 3. If 5 matches were played, the match points total $10$ and, being prime and at least 2 for each of five teams, are exactly $2$ each; but then the US could not be strictly ahead of Canada and Slovakia on points. So **7 matches** have been played and the 14 match points split as $5/3/2/2/2$ (all prime).

Four of the seven games are the three 2-0 results of the cycle and the 5-0 result: $6+5=11$ goals. The other three games share the remaining $17-11=6$ goals, each with a prime total of at least 2, so each has exactly 2 goals ($2$-$0$ or $1$-$1$). The team that drew all its games has a prime number $k\ge2$ of points, so there are at least two draws, and they are $1$-$1$. The US has 5 points, so its record is 2 wins, 1 draw, 1 loss. Because its goals for and against are both prime it cannot have been in the 5-0 game, so it won two games 2-0, lost to Finland 0-2 and drew 1-1. Canada likewise was not in the 5-0 game: it won 2-0 (the group of three is US, Canada, Finland: US beat Canada, Canada beat Finland, Finland beat US), drew 1-1 and lost 0-2. The 5-0 win must be by Slovakia (Russia drew all its games) over Finland. Sorting out the opponents (US 2-0 Slovakia, US 1-1 Russia, Canada 1-1 Russia) gives the table. The conditions check: points $5,3,2,2,2$, goals for $5,3,5,2,2$, goals against $3,3,2,2,7$, winning margins $2$ and $5$, Slovakia ahead of Russia on goal difference ($+3$ versus $0$), and Russia and Finland (2 points each) have not met. (A computer search over all score assignments confirms this is the only solution.)

The completed table is shown in the answer; the seven games are US-CAN 2-0, US-SLO 2-0, US-RUS 1-1, US-FIN 0-2, CAN-RUS 1-1, CAN-FIN 2-0, SLO-FIN 5-0.

**Answer:** see the table.
